reader_summary.headline: I discovered Coifin earlier this year when I asked Twitter for the best Bloomberg alternative.
reader_summary.overview: I discovered Coifin earlier this year when I asked Twitter for the best Bloomberg alternative, and the overwhelming winner was an intriguing new product called Coifin. Coiffin is a web-based platform that lets you analyze stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, and other assets all in one place. I now use it daily to track what's going on in the market, and I think if you try it, you will too.

key_points.text: Coifin has tons of high-quality data, powerful functionality, and a nice, clean interface.

thesis: This episode argues that Amazon (AMZN) is a superior investment to early-stage startups because it combines high growth with rational business principles, a decentralized structure, and the discipline to kill non-viable initiatives. Conversely, the speakers express a lack of conviction regarding other major tech companies like Meta, PayPal, Tesla, and RH, viewing them as part of a 'next wave' they do not believe in.

claims.claim: The speaker views Amazon as a superior investment compared to startups due to its high growth rate and rational business principles.
claims.quote: I regularly look at Amazon stock and think, why does anyone invest in startups? Why not just invest in a trillion and a half dollar public company that's growing faster than any of them.

claims.claim: Amazon is praised for its decentralized structure and rationality, growing at 40% while other big tech companies do not.
claims.quote: I think what's amazing about Amazon is they are so decentralized and are working on so many different things and they are, I don't know, you could almost argue that as an organization as a whole, one of their guiding principles is just rationality.

claims.claim: Amazon is described as a company that will do what makes sense and kill initiatives that do not make sense.
claims.quote: They will do what makes sense. And if things don't make sense, they'll kill it.

claims.claim: Amazon is noted for its ability to compete head-to-head with smaller companies using its scale advantages without hesitation.
claims.quote: If they decide to enter your space, they will do it with all the scale advantages that they have, and they will not let up.

claims.claim: Google's acquisition of Android was driven by the need to reduce the massive cost of paying Apple for default search engine status on iOS.
claims.quote: And Android, the reason why it was important for them to have a credible competitor against Apple is to basically just reduce this incredible cost burden.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions being right on the edge of the app stores launch in 2008 and creating an iPhone app in college.
claims.quote: I was so fortunate to be right on the edge of the app stores launch in 2008. And when I created my first iPhone app in college that Apple was kind enough not to have reminders on the iPhone.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that they do not have conviction in the things people talk about as the next wave, including Meta.
claims.quote: And people talk about defy now. And people talk about a lot of the things that could be this next wave. I don't have conviction in any of them.
